title: Quant safelist, calibration harness, and catalog rollout runbook
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Introduce a safelist/guardrail layer in the model catalog that recommends per-model quantization profiles (FP8/INT8 variants) and a reproducible calibration + validation harness. Deliverables: safelist + blacklist rules, a calibration CI job and runbook, automated validation checks, and a catalog field for the recommended default profile and risk tier.
background: Teams want deterministic guidance for which quant profiles are safe to expose as defaults in the catalog. Past efforts produced quant presets and calibration notes, but we lack a standard harness to (a) run calibration offline, (b) validate output fidelity at scale, and (c) publish a single recommended profile with explicit guardrails (rollback thresholds, telemetry signals). This ticket defines the runbook to add per-model defaults and the safety net required for hosted and Dedicated offerings.
proposed_solution: 1) Define a catalog field: recommended_quant_profile (e.g., fp8-e4m3, int8-across-channel), risk_tier (low/medium/high), and calibration_artifact_digest. 2) Build a reusable calibration harness (calib-harness) that: performs offline activation range collection, runs per-layer symmetric/asymmetric quant calibration, computes KL/MAE statistics, and exports a calibration cache. 3) Integrate a validation pipeline: automated quality metrics, latency/cost delta, and a lightweight human A/B sampling for high-risk models. 4) Implement safelist rules: only models with pass metrics can have a default applied; high-risk models must be manual review. 5) Expose telemetry: token-level quality delta, highest-deviation prompt buckets, and cost-per-token estimates for the profile.
calibration_workflow: Step 1: Dataset selection - use a reserved calibration corpus per model (min 2k sequences, stratified by length and task: generation, instruction, embeddings). Step 2: FP32 baseline run to collect activation histograms and KV statistics. Step 3: Apply candidate profiles - FP8 (e4m3), FP8 (e5m2), INT8 symmetric, INT8 per-channel. Step 4: For each profile produce: per-layer KL divergence, activation MAE, output token distribution delta, and latency/cost estimate. Step 5: If KL < 0.015 and MAE < 1e-2 and generation-similarity >= 98% (see validation_plan), mark as pass. Step 6: Archive calibration artifacts and publish calibration_artifact_digest to catalog. CI: calibration job re-runs on model weight updates or every 30 days for hosted models.
validation_plan: Automated checks: a) Perplexity change on held-out evaluation suite (threshold: <= 2% relative increase). b) NLG metrics where applicable (BLEU/ROUGE/ROUGE-L/ExactMatch thresholds per model family). c) Synthetic regression tests with 300 edge-case prompts (no >5% token-level deviation allowed). d) Latency regression: 95th percentile increase capped at 10ms for short sequences. e) Cost delta estimation: must reduce tokens CPU/GPU cost by >10% to be considered. Human review: for models flagged high-risk, sample 200 outputs A/B vs FP32; require no statistically significant preference for FP32 at p<0.05. Safety checks: run safety classifier on generated outputs and require no increase in toxic/sensitive content rates beyond baseline +/-0.1%. If any check fails, profile cannot be recommended by default.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal canary - apply recommended profile to a synthetic route running 0% real traffic; verify telemetry. Phase 1: Canary to 3% of non-critical traffic for 48 hours, monitor quality and errors. Phase 2: Gradual increase to 25% over 7 days if metrics stable. Phase 3: Full catalog default assignment and UI exposure. Rollback triggers: validation metric regressions exceed thresholds, safety drift, or customer incidents. For Dedicated/private installs, catalog exposes recommended profile but does not auto-apply without customer opt-in.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Calibration harness implemented and reproducible with documented inputs/outputs. 2) CI calibration job runs end-to-end for at least three model families and publishes calibration_artifact_digest. 3) Validation pipeline enforces thresholds and blocks profiles that fail checks. 4) Catalog schema extended with recommended_quant_profile, risk_tier, calibration_artifact_digest, and exposure is visible in the Console. 5) Runbook and rollback playbook published in Confluence and linked from the ticket. 6) Telemetry dashboards created showing token-level quality delta, cost delta, and top-10 prompt buckets by deviation.
open_questions: Do we allow per-customer overrides of recommended_quant_profile and how do we track their liability/QA?
What privacy restrictions apply to storing calibration corpora for closed-source customer models?
Should calibration re-run be triggered by model minor version bumps or only major weight changes?
Is the human review sample size (200) sufficient for large generation models, or should it be proportional to model family?
updates: 2025-02-01: Ticket created by Ayesha Patel to centralize calibration runbook and safelist rules.
2025-02-04: Spike completed - prototype harness can produce per-layer KL and activation histograms (branch: github.com/redwood-inference/calib-harness #PR-427).
2025-02-07: Meeting with Product and DX - agreed to add risk_tier field and require manual review for 'high' tier models.
2025-02-12: First CI job wired up on CI runner (calib-job) and ran for two small models; artifacts uploaded to S3 (s3://redwood-calib/ENG-27654/).
2025-02-15: QA added validation thresholds; draft Confluence runbook at https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Quant+Calibration+Runbook v0.1
notes: Trade-offs considered: full per-layer retraining vs calibration-only approach (we prefer calibration-only to keep compute cost low). We considered using only KL divergence but added MAE and synthetic prompt buckets because KL can miss tail-case token errors. For models with narrow dynamic ranges (some gated-linear layers), we plan to default to conservative int8-per-channel profiles or require manual sign-off. Long-term: explore learned quantization-aware fine-tuning as a follow-up project.
